We have not yet completed end-to-end testing with assistive technologies and users with disabilities. We therefore do not claim full WCAG conformance. Our design approach We use WCAG 2.2 Level AA as our technical design goal. We also follow the Canada.ca Content Style Guide and plain-language guidance when writing and organizing the site. This independent project does not claim to be a Government of Canada website. Use the language buttons to switch between English and French summaries. Use the skip link to move to the main content. Search and filter tables using labeled controls and your keyboard. Read numerical findings as text without relying on charts or colour. Use the source link in each record to check the original evidence. Known limitations Some original research documents are only available in English, and some external PDFs may not be fully accessible. We provide French summaries of our catalogue records, not translations of every original document. Downloaded CSV files contain technical column names in English. passage: Representation and changes in the benchmark La représentation et l’évolution du repère Representation and changes in the benchmark Representation is compared with workforce availability, the benchmark used under the Employment Equity Act . From the March 31, 2024 data, Treasury Board bases workforce availability on the 2021 Census and the 2022 Canadian Survey on Disability. For racialized (visible minority) employees, the benchmark rose from 17.3% to 22.7%. An organization’s representation can rise while its gap to the updated benchmark also grows. This page explains the change and how to describe results. How to read this The bar shows the actual result. The tick or benchmark shows the comparison point. A gap is the difference between a result and its benchmark. Suppressed data means the count is too small to publish. It does not mean zero. Read this with related data before drawing conclusions. Context Representation can rise while the gap to the benchmark grows, when the benchmark itself changes. Compare the gap as well as the number of employees. Check next Overview · Salary DI tracker · Demographic gaps · Use these figures in a briefing note o La représentation est comparée à la disponibilité au sein de la population active, le repère utilisé en vertu de la Loi sur l’équité en matière d’emploi. À partir des données au 31 mars 2024, le Conseil du Trésor fonde la disponibilité sur le Recensement de 2021 et l’Enquête canadienne sur l’incapacité de 2022. Pour les employés racisés (minorités visibles), le repère est passé de 17,3 % à 22,7 %. La représentation d’une organisation peut augmenter alors que son écart par rapport au repère mis à jour s’accroît aussi. Cette page explique ce changement et la façon de décrire les résultats. Comment lire ceci La barre montre le résultat réel. Le repère montre le point de comparaison. Un écart est la différence entre un résultat et son repère. Une donnée supprimée signifie que le dénombrement est trop petit pour être publié. Cela ne veut pas dire zéro. Lisez ceci avec les données connexes avant de tirer des conclusions. passage: Staffing fairness and barriers: 2025 survey Équité en dotation et obstacles : sondage 2025 PUBLIC SERVICE DATA · 2025 Staffing fairness and barriers: 2025 survey What federal employees reported about staffing fairness, bias, assessment and accommodation in the 2025 Staffing and Non-Partisanship Survey (SNPS). These results describe respondents across organizations subject to the Public Service Employment Act . They are not results for any one department. There were 82,987 respondents, a response rate of 30.9%. Surveyed June 5 to August 14, 2025. Questions about past staffing experiences generally refer to April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2025. Results are adjusted for non-response. Ces résultats décrivent les répondants des organisations assujetties à la Loi sur l’emploi dans la fonction publique. Ce ne sont pas les résultats d’un ministère en particulier. Il y a eu 82 987 répondants, soit un taux de réponse de 30,9 %. Sondage mené du 5 juin au 14 août 2025. passage: Methodology and audit trail Methodology and audit trail Methodology and audit trail Figures in this tool come from published sources, mainly from the Government of Canada. Where a figure is calculated or estimated, this is stated. This page records, for each dataset, its source, how it was processed, and what it can and cannot support, so the work can be checked and reproduced. Principles Numbers are copied verbatim from official tables. Where a value was derived (for example, summing salary bands), the calculation is noted and was checked against published totals. Suppressed cells are left suppressed. They are never estimated, interpolated or filled. No organization's data is matched to a different organization. Where a name could not be matched across datasets, the cell is left blank. Survey differences and correlations show where to look further. They do not establish causes. Datasets used Provenance and handling for each dataset in this tool. Lorsqu’un chiffre est calculé ou estimé, cela est indiqué. Cette page présente, pour chaque jeu de données, sa source, son traitement et ce qu’il permet ou non d’établir, afin que le travail puisse être vérifié et reproduit. Les chiffres sont copiés textuellement des tableaux officiels. Lorsqu'une valeur a été dérivée (par exemple, la somme de tranches salariales), le calcul est indiqué et a été vérifié par rapport aux totaux publiés. Les cellules supprimées le restent. Elles ne sont jamais estimées, interpolées ni remplies. Les données d'une organisation ne sont jamais associées à une autre organisation. Lorsqu'un nom n'a pu être apparié entre les jeux de données, la cellule est laissée vide. Les écarts et les corrélations du sondage indiquent où regarder de plus près. passage: Salary disproportionality index, 2017 to 2025 Indice de disproportion salariale, de 2017 à 2025 Salary disproportionality index, 2017 to 2025 The Disproportionality Index (DI) compares a group’s presence in a salary range with that of all employees. A DI of 1.0 means a group is in that salary range at the same rate as all employees. Above 1.0 means overrepresented in that range; below 1.0 means underrepresented. These are the published figures of the independent Disproportionality Index project, derived from Treasury Board diversity and inclusion statistics. How to read this The bar shows the actual result. The tick or benchmark shows the comparison point. A gap is the difference between a result and its benchmark. Suppressed data means the count is too small to publish. It does not mean zero. Read this with related data before drawing conclusions. Context An index above 1.0 in lower ranges and below 1.0 in higher ranges means that a group is concentrated in lower salaries. passage: Limitations of the data Limites des données Limitations of the data What this public data can and cannot show. Read this before drawing conclusions. The results describe differences between groups and between organizations. They do not show the cause of a difference, and they do not show that discrimination occurred. What this data does not show Public datasets may not show process-level barriers (who decided what, and how). Suppressed values do not mean zero; they mean the count was too small to publish. Self-identification is voluntary, so representation may understate the true numbers. A department's own workforce availability may differ from the public-service-wide benchmark, reflecting its occupations and region. Data may not include branch, region, classification, occupational group, language profile, security level, or process stage. Some questions require additional departmental data before conclusions can be drawn. Limites des données Ce que ces données publiques peuvent et ne peuvent pas montrer. À lire avant de tirer des conclusions. Les résultats décrivent des différences entre les groupes et entre les organisations. Ils ne montrent pas la cause d’une différence ni qu’il y a eu discrimination. Ce que ces données ne montrent pas Les jeux de données publics peuvent ne pas montrer les obstacles au niveau des processus (qui a décidé quoi, et comment). Les valeurs supprimées ne signifient pas zéro; elles signifient que le dénombrement était trop petit pour être publié. L'auto-identification est volontaire; la représentation peut donc sous-estimer les nombres réels. La disponibilité au sein de la population active propre à un ministère peut différer du repère pangouvernemental, selon ses professions et sa région. Les données peuvent ne pas inclure la direction, la région, la classification, le groupe professionnel, le profil linguistique, le niveau de sécurité ou l'étape du processus. Certaines questions exigent des données ministérielles supplémentaires avant de pouvoir tirer des conclusions.

The overall figure hides differences. The findings below show where women who also belong to another group report different experiences, and where the published data stops. Les femmes représentent 56,8 % de l’administration publique centrale (151 528 employées au 31 mars 2025), au-dessus de leur estimation de disponibilité au sein de la population active de 54,9 %. Ce chiffre global cache des différences. Les constats ci-dessous montrent où les femmes qui appartiennent aussi à un autre groupe font état d’expériences différentes, et où s’arrêtent les données publiées. Women are the majority of each other designated group: 62.1% of Indigenous employees, 60.4% of persons with disabilities, 57.3% of members of visible minorities and 57.3% of Black employees are women (March 31, 2025). Results published for those groups describe groups that are mostly women. See the figures . In the 2022 employee survey, 19% of women with a disability said they had been harassed at work in the past 12 months, compared with 9% of women without a disability. passage: Call to Action: what the data point to Appel à l’action : ce que les données indiquent From 2021 to 2024, what organizations reported moved from training and plans to sponsorship and data. Most recruitment goals were set by organizations already at or above availability, and the group most often below availability was outside the goal question. Where organizations reported bias or anti-racism training, fewer racialized employees said they faced bias in staffing. Where organizations reported self-identification campaigns, representation of persons with disabilities rose more. Where 2021 letters described leadership or talent development programs, employees’ views of the Call to Action fell more by 2024. Where organizations named Black employees in their documents, more employees overall said the Call to Action had a positive impact, and fewer Black employees did. Where a racialized recruitment goal was set, racialized employees were as likely as their colleagues to see opportunities for promotion. Where organizations reported an employment systems review, more employees said the Call to Action had a positive impact. Representation changed by about the same amount after 2023 whether or not an organization had set a recruitment goal. Organizations that described targeted recruitment in 2021 did not see clearly larger gains in representation or hiring. Organizations that reported sponsorship programs did not show clearly better views of promotion opportunities among racialized or Black employees. Organizations that reported equity commitments in executive performance agreements did not show clearly more positive views of the Call to Action. De 2021 à 2024, les déclarations des organisations sont passées de la formation et des plans au parrainage et aux données. La plupart des objectifs de recrutement ont été fixés par des organisations qui atteignaient déjà la disponibilité, et le groupe le plus souvent sous la disponibilité ne faisait pas partie de la question sur les objectifs.
